metas.name: United Kingdom  - Western Isles sticker
metas.note: These colourful stickers are found in the Western Isles. Their very rarely seen since these islands are mostly rural without lampposts, but they can be seen commonly in Stornoway, and occasionally elsewhere too.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - A1 Roads
metas.note:
The main A-roads in the UK are grouped by their first digit after the A, for example A380 will be located in the southwest of the country.

Beware that A-roads starting with any digit from 1 to 8 can also be found in Northern Ireland.

Tip: Imagine the UK as a clock, the digits go clockwise, starting at 1 and ending at 9.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Aberdeenshire + Aberdeen street sign
metas.note: This street sign is unique to Aberdeenshire and Aberdeen. Its blue with white capitalized text and does not have any border around it.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Bedford sticker
metas.note: This unique sticker with the black eagle logo on top is found in Bedford and areas around it.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Belfast mountains
metas.note:
Depending where you are in Belfast, you can often see these distinct mountains/hills with lots of trees on it (gets more bald on the top) to the west/north-west, sometimes with 1 or 2 towers on top of it. Hills can also be seen in the east/south east.

If your not sure these mountains are the Belfast mountains, check for clues to confirm your in Northern Ireland and it will 100% be Belfast.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Bin - City name
metas.note: Bins in urban areas often have the city name on them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Birmingham - phone code 0121
metas.note:
Landline phone numbers in the UK always have nine or ten digits after the 0 trunk code. The first two to four digits after the 0 are the area code. Unfortunately for Geoguessr players, there is not much rhyme or reason to their geographic ordering.

However, the area codes of some large cities are still worth memorising. The most important ones are summarised in this infographic. Notably, all of Northern Ireland uses the phone code 028, and all of London uses 020.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Birmingham yellow tape/paint
metas.note: The majority of poles and signposts in Birmingham have either yellow tape or yellow paint wrapped around them. Lampposts will also usually have this yellow sticker.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Blue stickers
metas.note:
Blue stickers/stickers with blue in them (excluding blue letters/numbers) are found in North Wales.

If you want, you can learn which blue stickers are found in which region:

  • Light blue stickers are found in Anglesey.
  • Green white dark blue stickers are found in Denbighshire.
  • Purple white light blue stickers are found in Conwy.
  • Generic blue stickers are found in Flintshire, Wrexham and Gwynedd, they are very rare in Gwynedd and are mostly found in Flintshire and Wrexham (east part of North Wales).

Other blue stickers can also be occasionally seen in North Wales.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Boat trekker
metas.note: Boat trekkers are limited to three locations: the River Thames, which runs through London, Keyhaven Lake, and Loch Ness lake. Each have different boats and very different landscapes.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Bristol street sign
metas.note: Street signs in Bristol will always have ''BS'' with a number written on the right side. This one is easy to remember because BS stands for Bri-Stol.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Cambridgeshire + Coventry + Derby + South Tyneside sticker
metas.note:
This white sticker with black letters and numbers and a diamond with small text under it is found in Cambridgeshire, Coventry, Derby and South Tyneside.

Cambridgeshire + Coventry have 6 or less letters/numbers and white space between the text and diamond.

Derby always has 7 letters/numbers and no space between the text and diamond.

South Tyneside always has a blue sticker under it.

NOTE: This excludes Peterborough which has its own sticker, which always has ''PCC" written on a white sticker.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Cardiff - phone number 029
metas.note:

However, the area codes of some large cities are still worth memorising. The most important ones are summarised in this infographic. Notably, all of Northern Ireland uses the phone code 028, and all of London uses 020.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Castle stone walls
metas.note: Stone walls that look like a castle wall are mostly found in North Wales. Especially towards Anglesey and in Anglesey. They can also sometimes be found elsewhere in Wales.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Ceredigion sticker
metas.note: This yellow sticker, sometimes white, with 3 numbers and 4 numbers under it can be found in Ceredigion. What makes it extra distinct, is that its pasted on another white sticker behind it.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Cornish palms
metas.note: Cornish palms (Cordyline australis) in the UK are most commonly found in the far southwest along the coast and in Jersey. Although, they can rarely be found all along the west coast up to Scotland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Cornwall plate
metas.note: This very distinctive black plate with a letter followed by 3 numbers is commonly found in Cornwall. The letter and numbers are always either white or yellow, sometimes mixed together.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Cumbria architecture
metas.note:
In Cumbria, especially around Keswick often has these white houses with black ladder-like frames on the corners, often with black frames around the windows.

NOTE: These frames can be found elsewhere
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Cylindrical hay bales
metas.note: Cylindrical hay bales laying around on these hilly agricultural fields can mostly be found in the region north of Aberdeen. They can very rarely be seen elsewhere in Scotland.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Dark red bricks architecture
metas.note:
North West England around Manchester/Lancashire has a lot of dark red bricks. Dark brown, black and white doors are common, aswell as black and white lintels around windows are often seen.

NOTE: Dark red bricks can be found elsewhere too.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Distinct stone walls
metas.note:
Houses and walls that are made out of pebble stones or flint stones with red brick build in to them are found in East Anglia, most commonly in Norfolk, they can also be found on the south of Sussex and East Sussex.

These stones can rarely have a different color like yellow or black.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.note:

metas.name: United Kingdom - Fife Sticker
metas.note: This white sticker with 2 black numbers and 3 pieces of small text, 1 above the number and 2 under it, can be found in Fife.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Flat Fens landscape
metas.note: Eastern England tends to be more flat. The Fens area of reclaimed land has very distinct "Dutch-like" landscape. Its typically very flat and open, with straight roads and small dikes, often hedgerows absent. The area around the town Goole also features a similar landscape.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Flat landscape with big hedgerows
metas.note:
It is very common to see big hedgerows in north eastern Anglia, combined with its very flat landscape, most likely will be around that area.

NOTE: Its also common to see just normal hedgerows in this region, having normal hedgrows with flat landscape is still a good clue for this region.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.note: This pink sticker with the text ''PEOPLE MAKE GLASGOW'' can be found on these trash bins in Glasgow.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Glasgow street sign
metas.note: Glasgow street signs are white with a black frame in it.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Gravel front gardens
metas.note: Lincolnshire, Norfolk and the Fens commonly have bungalows with neat gravel front gardens.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Greater London bus stop sign
metas.note: This bus stop sign is found in Greater London. It has a very distinct logo on the top half.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Greater Manchester bus stop sign
metas.note:
This busstop sign can be found in Greater Manchester, it has the phone code on it and the M logo on the top left corner with a bunch of other things like a bee on the right. The logo's and phone code can only be seen on one side.

NOTE: A different version can be seen in older coverage, which will be completely white with a huge M logo on it.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Hampshire and West Sussex sticker
metas.note: This white sticker with 1 - 2 numbers and lots of small text with a logo under it is found in Hampshire and West Sussex. Sometimes there is also text and a logo above the number, or there is only text without a number.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Hebrides Islands
metas.note: The areas around the Hebrides Islands often have a rocky, treeless tundra-like landscape, but is by far mostly seen in the Western Isles.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Industrial buildings
metas.note: Urban areas in the Midlands, especially around the Black Country and Birmingham, often have a very industrial appearance. This region is well known for its history of heavy industry, with factories, warehouses, and old brick buildings.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Isle of Man - Gen 2 cam
metas.note:
Coverage on the Isle of Man is limited to Generation 2.

This camera can be recognized by the lower camera quality and circular blur above and below. Colours will also seem slightly off.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Isle of Man - Isle of Man licence plate
metas.note: Similar to the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man uses white front licence plates with yellow rears, but with a red strip on the left.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Isle of Man - Striped kerbs
metas.note: Striped kerbs can sometimes be seen along main roads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Kielder Forest
metas.note: The Kielder Forest and some areas around it is filled with dense pine trees. While pine trees can be seen in other places as well, no other region has them in the same abundance as the Kielder Forest.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Lake District
metas.note: The Lake District is very hilly, with a lot of exposed rocks and stone walls. It can look like the Scottish Highlands, but Scotland is generally less rocky.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.note: Street signs in Leeds District will always have ''LS'' with a number written on the right side. This one is easy to remember because LS stands for Leed-S.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Leicestershire pole plate
metas.note:
This black plate with 1 - 3 numbers, useally yellow, is found in Leicestershire. They look like Northern Ireland stickers but those are flat instead of a plate and have no supports around the pole.

NOTE: For some odd reason, they very rarely appear in Leicester itself.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Limestone architecture
metas.note: This golden colored Limestone is very common in and around Cotswold, especially towards the north.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Lincolnshire sticker
metas.note:
Yellow stickers with ''LCC'' (which stands for ''Lincolnshire County Council'') written under the numbers can be found in Lincolnshire. ''LCC" can sometimes be hard to see, if you only see ''CC" clearly, that also confirms your in Lincolnshire.

NOTE: This doesn’t apply to North Lincolnshire and North East Lincolnshire (Scunthorpe, Grimsby and surrounding areas) which are separate councils.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.note: Liverpool street signs often an L on the bottom right corner, standing for Liverpool, towards the centre in the city you will get signs with a unique shape and often have the text ''City of Liverpool'' written on them.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - London - Gen 4 white electric vehicle
metas.note:
Some of the Generation 4 coverage in London and surrounding areas was taken by a white electric vehicle, with this distinct back of the car visible.

NOTE: A similar car was used in Dublin and Germany, so make sure to check out other clues as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - London street signs
metas.note: London street signs have a distinct look. They usually feature the street name in black, followed by the postcode and borough in red.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Mansions
metas.note: Wealthy areas in the UK are often in the Home Counties near London, especially Surrey and Berkshire, where you’ll find big houses and gated mansions along leafy roads.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - New Forest landscape
metas.note: The New Forest has a distinctive look, with a mix of forest and heathland landscape.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Newcastle architecture
metas.note: In urban areas around Newcastle, it’s common to see red brick walls extending from houses to enclose gardens. These walls often include garage doors built into them.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - North York Moors
metas.note: North York Moors has a distinct moorland landscape. Features rolling, mostly brown moorlands, with rough grasses and patches of low vegetation
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Northern Ireland - Black sticker with yellow text
metas.note:
These black stickers with yellow text sometimes appear on lampposts in Northern Ireland.

NOTE: Wiltshire have the same stickers on lamposts, so be aware of that.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Northern Ireland - phone number 028
metas.note:

metas.name: United Kingdom - Northern Ireland - Rounded edge gate
metas.note: Gates in Northern Ireland have these rounded edges, unlike mainland UK which have square edges.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Northern Ireland warning sticker
metas.note: Warning stickers in Northern Ireland are almost always fully wrapped around the pole. Unlike mainland UK, which commonly uses just 1 or 2 stickers on the pole.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Orange tape
metas.note: In Northamptonshire, you can often find orange tape wrapped around poles. A white sticker with blue text and numbers and a diamond shaped icon on it can commonly be seen aswell on the poles.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Orkney Islands
metas.note: The Orkney islands is mostly treeless and open, with vast farmland in many places and mostly small hills.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Pennines architecture
metas.note: Pennines areas of Yorkshire and Lancashire often have this very distinctive dark gritstone with patches of black on the bricks. Their also more common towards the south.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Perth and Kinross sticker
metas.note: This white sticker with a black letter and 4 numbers, and has "FAULT'' with a phone number written under it is found in Perth and Kinross. Most of the times, it has a small frame in the sticker around the text.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - QR code sticker
metas.note: This distinctive yellow sticker features a 6 number code followed by a QR code. This is a great clue that you are in the counties north of London. As it has consistently only been found in the following counties: Norfolk, Suffolk, Essex, Cambridgeshire, Bedfordshire, Hertfordshire and Buckinghamshire. It is frequently found on rural wooden electricity poles.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Red roofs
metas.note: Eastern UK can have these very distinct red clay pantile roofs, especially on older houses. This is commonly found on the eastern half of the coast from Fife down to East Anglia.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scotland - Houses made of large blocks of sandstone or granite
metas.note: It is common to see houses made of large blocks of sandstone or granite in Scotland. Granite buildings are common in Aberdeen, red sandstone is common in Glasgow and Dumfries, and yellow sandstone is common in Edinburgh.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scotland - Passing place sign
metas.note: These ‘Passing Place’ signs are 95% found in Scotland. Wales has Welsh written under it and the England version is the same.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scotland - Red and white bollards
metas.note:
In Scotland, you can often find these red and white bollards. They are round, bulky, and have a red-and-grey reflector that wraps all the way around.

They are sometimes found in other parts of the UK.

NOTE: The bollard looks similar to the French one. However, there are some small differences. For example, the Scottish bollard is round on the top, while the French one is more spiked.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scotland - Scottish Gaelic
metas.note:
Scottish Gaelic is a Celtic language that is closely related to Irish. They have a very similar look and use accent marks commonly. Common and recognizable letter clusters include bh, dh, fh, mh, ai, ea, eo, and ui.

Scottish Gaelic on road signs is found most commonly in the Scottish Highlands, and is almost always found north of Glasgow.

NOTE: Scottish Gaelic on road signs will often be in green or yellow text. This will not happen with Welsh or Irish on road signs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scottish Highlands
metas.note:
The Scottish Highlands can be distinguished by the semi-barren, very mountainous landscape.

NOTE: A lot of Generation 4 coverage in the Highlands is from (early) spring, meaning that the vegetation often looks brown and yellow.

In addition, some of the most mountainous parts of Wales and Northern England can look similar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scottish Highlands - Northern region
metas.note: Within the Scottish Highlands, the northern part of it is much less mountainous than the rest of the highlands. It has mostly just hills, with sometimes a few or less mountains visible in the distance.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Seagull
metas.note: This is Gulliver the Seagull. If you see him, you will be in Colwyn Bay.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Sheffield - phone number 0114
metas.note:
Landline phone numbers in the UK always have nine or ten digits after the 0 trunk code. The first two to four digits after the 0 are the area code. Unfortunately for Geoguessr players, there is not much rhyme or reason to their geographic ordering.

However, the area codes of some large cities are still worth memorising. The most important ones are summarised in this infographic. Notably, all of Northern Ireland uses the phone code 028, and all of London uses 020.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United kingdom - Shetland Islands
metas.note: You can recognize the Shetland Islands by the very low amount of vegetation and useally no trees at all. Patches of trees can rarely be seen on these islands. You will never see mountains either, its all just hills with mostly grass and some small bushes. Some parts also look like the Faroe Islands.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Snowdonia
metas.note:
Some roads, mostly in the south and north Snowdonia, have these distinct dark grey stone walls with vertical stones on top of it along the road. The landscape itself is very forested and mountainous, but less forested in the north east.

NOTE: These stone walls can be found elsewhere too, most commonly in North Wales.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - South east Northern Ireland region
metas.note: This small region all the way south of ''mourne area of outstanding natural beauty'' features slightly hilly landscape with lots of rockwalls and distinct mountains to the north, further west there will be hedgerows instead of rockwalls but the same mountains can still be seen.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - South West England architecture
metas.note:
South West England, especially Cornwall and Devon, features a lot of stone and light pastel buildings. These materials are sometimes mixed together so they feature both materials in one building.

NOTE: Wales can sometimes look similar so check for other clues (if available) to confirm your in South West England.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Southampton street sign
metas.note: Street signs in Southampton almost always have the text ''City of Southampton'' written on them. This meta is super easy to know because it literally just says the city name on it and these signs can be find everywhere in the city.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Southern Wales valley architecture
metas.note:
This valley north-west of Cardiff has a very recognizable look. Featuring many terraced houses and brown stone walls with colorful windows and often have this unique shape made out of pastel around the windows and doors. The towns are build on hills so its always hilly.

NOTE: Similar valleys with the same look can be find elsewhere in Wales but this one is by far the biggest.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Stone walls
metas.note:
The Lake District, North Pennines, Yorkshire Dales, Nidderdale and Peak District are very hilly and have alot of stone walls. Stone walls can appear in other national parks and places but not as much as these 5 national parks, which have the majority of stone walls.

The Lake District is by far the hilliest, with plenty of exposed rock. Along with the North Pennines and Yorkshire Dales, it sometimes features abandoned-looking barns. Beyond that, I’m not sure how to tell them apart.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Suffolk sticker
metas.note: This white sticker with blue numbers and letters and commonly a phone number under it can be found in Suffolk.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - T shape sticker
metas.note: A white sticker with numbers forming a T shape, can be found in Pembrokeshire and Carmarthenshire.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Thatched roofs
metas.note: Thatched roofs are the most common in the middle of southern England, especially around Hampshire and Wiltshire.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Tudor architecture
metas.note: Tudor architecture, mostly black and white, sometimes with red bricks mixed are mostly found in West Midlands and East Anglia. They can also be found in Wales, mostly towards the England border. They can also be quite common in the south like Kent and Sussex and sometimes parts of Surrey and Oxfordshire. They can very rarely be found in Northern England and almost never in Scotland.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Twenty’s Plenty speed signs
metas.note: Speed signs with green borders with the text “Twenty’s Plenty” are mostly found in and around Glasgow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Wales - ARAF road marking
metas.note:
In Wales, markings on the road are in both English and Welsh. One of the best examples of this is ‘Araf’, which means ‘Slow’. This marking is only found in Wales.

NOTE: Araf is not the only Welsh language marking you can find, it is just the most common. Whenever you see an obviously non-English marking next to an English one, consider guessing in Wales.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Wales - Roadline gap
metas.note: Gaps in roadlines are most commonly found in Wales.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Wales - Welsh language
metas.note:
Welsh is a Celtic language that is spoken throughout Wales. Road signs in Wales are usually bilingual English and Welsh. Towns often have Welsh names too. Welsh uses the letters D, W, and Y much more commonly than English. The double LL is also very distinct.

NOTE: Scottish Gaelic and Irish are both also Celtic languages. They can look somewhat similar to Welsh.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Wales architecture
metas.note:
Many Welsh towns have a mix of stone and pastel buildings, often with colorfull paint around doors and windows. This is especially common in the western parts near the coast.

NOTE: South West England can sometimes look similar so check for other clues (if available) to confirm your in Wales.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Wales sheep
metas.note: Sheep are most common in Wales, but can be found elsewhere too. So if you see a bunch of sheep and its very hilly/mountainous with typical Wale-ish landscape, with many hedgerows and green grassy fields and you have no other clues, you might aswell guess Wales.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Weald Hanging tiles
metas.note: Weald Hanging tiles are the most common in Sussex and Kent. But can sometimes be found elsewhere in the southern half of England.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - West Midlands County bus stop sign
metas.note: This bus stop sign is found in West Midlands County. It has a very distinct logo on the top half.
metas.footer: For more info, check out the UK Plonkit and scroll down to Maps and resources.

metas.name: United Kingdom - West Northern Ireland - Green text
metas.note:
Signs with green text underneath the street name, indicating the townland, can be found in the western part of Northern Ireland.

Especially towards the north of the shaded area, there may be a metal divider between the two lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.
